) Then once, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [riding] a superb chariot adorned

with the finest sandalwood, covered with the skins of lions, tigers, and leopards, yoked
to four

Thus

children.text: m ukte bodhisatvo laghulaghv eva tasmād rathavarād avatīrya hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditahṛdayas tebhyo dvijātibhyas taṃ rathavaram upadarśayann uvāca

children.translated_text: 'Just as this chariot was given by me to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with supreme joy,

children.text: tathāhaṃ tribhavaṃ tyaktvā spṛśeyaṃ bodhim uttamām //
children.translated_text: so may I, having renounced the three realms of existence, attain the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)!'
[<s>Viśv</s> 12]

children.text: ) so 'pareṇa samayena kundakumudahimarajatasitābhravarṇaṃ saptasujātasupratiṣṭhitacaraṇatalaṃ airāvaṇadviradavilāsagāminaṃ parasvābhāvyalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaṃ puṇyadarśanaṃ rājyavardhanaṃ nāma gajavaram adhiruhya parituṣṭabhṛtyamitrasevakānuyātrikaiś candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauṃcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīva
children.translated_text: ) At another time, [he rode out on] the excellent elephant named <s>Rājyavardhana</s> ('Increaser of the Kingdom'), of the color of <s>kunda</s> flowers, white water lilies, snow, silver, and white clouds, with seven well-born and firmly-set feet, moving with the grace of <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, adorned with the marks of an incomparable natural disposition, auspicious to behold,
[he rode]
out to the park grounds, whose groves resounded with the cries of <s>jīvaka</s> birds,
[the park grounds]
he went forth. (
[<s>Viśv</s> 13]

children.text: ) atha kecit pratyarthikaprayuktā viprā vedavedāṃgavidas tvaritatvaritaṃ viśvantarakumāram abhigamyocuḥ: jayatu bhavāṃ kṣatriyakumāra ity āha ca
children.translated_text: ) Then certain <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, sent by rivals, learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, quickly approached prince <s>Viśvantara</s> and said: 'May the <s>kṣatriya</s> prince be victorious!' And they said:
'In the worlds of demons, immortals, and men, you are renowned as a giver of everything.

children.text: dātum enaṃ{d} gajavaram asmabhyas tvam ihārhasi //

most swiftly descending

children.text: tathāhaṃ tribhavaṃ tyaktvā spṛśeyaṃ bodhim uttamām //
children.translated_text: so may I, having renounced the three realms of existence, attain the supreme awakening!'

(

[<s>Viśv</s> 16]

children.text: ) kumāraḥ pitrā parityaktaś cintayāmāsa: bodhāya mayā kṛtavyavasāyena sarvalokānugrahārthaṃ baddhasannāhena gajo 'sau tyaktas
children.translated_text: ) The prince, abandoned by his father, reflected: 'Having resolved upon awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), having girded myself for the benefit of all the world, that elephant was given away by me.'
'While dwelling in the home, one should give gifts according to one's ability;

children.text: tapovanaṃ vā saṃśṛtya kartavyo niyamaḥ paraḥ //
children.translated_text: or, having resorted to the forest of austerities, one should undertake the supreme discipline.'
'Therefore I shall abandon the home and go to the forest of austerities;

children.text: vaktuṃ na tūtsahe vākyaṃ na dāsyāmīti yācakaṃ //
children.translated_text: but I cannot bring myself to say the words "I will not give" to a suppliant.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 17]

children.text: ) athaivaṃ kṛtamatir bodhisatvo bhāryāyā mādryāḥ sakāśaṃ abhigamyaitad vistareṇa nivedayāmāsa. tato mādrī sahaśravaṇād eva priyaviprayogāśaṃkitahṛdayā kṛtakarapuṭā bodhisatvam uvāca: āryaputra yady evam ahaṃ api tapovanaṃ yāsyāmi. na śakyaṃ mayā āryaputraviyuktayā m
children.translated_text: ) Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having thus made up his mind, went to his wife <s>Mādrī</s> and informed her of this in detail. Then <s>Mādrī</s>, upon hearing this, her heart anxious with the fear of separation from her beloved, with palms joined, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Noble son, if even
for
a moment I cannot sustain my life. How so?'

children.text: gaganam iva candravihīnaṃ sasyavihīnā bhaved yathā pṛthivī /
children.translated_text: 'Like the sky without the moon, like the earth without crops,

children.text: nalinīva jalavihīnā bhartṛvihīnā tathā bhaven nārī //
children.translated_text: like a lotus pond without water — so would a woman be without her husband.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 18]

children.text: ) bodhisatva uvāca: avaśyam evāvayor ante viyogena bhavitavyaṃ. eṣa hi lokasvabhāvaḥ. tvaṃ ca pravarānnapānaśa
children.translated_text: ) The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Inevitably, at the end, there must be separation between us. This is the nature of the world. And you, accustomed to the finest food, drink, bed,
seat,
and
garments,
your body
exceedingly

children.translated_text: delicate — in the forest of austerities you would have to sleep on ground covered with grass and leaves, eat roots, flowers, and fruits, walk on terrain strewn with <s>darbha</s> grass, stones, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and thorns, and endure frequent fasting; and one's self [must be given] to all people —
[given]

children.text:
punar api tāvat saṃpradhāryatām iti.
mādrī kathayaty āryaputra yathāśaktyāham āryaputrasya anuvartiṣyāmīti.
bodhisatvaḥ kathayati yady evaṃ smartavyā te iyaṃ pratijñeti.
(
children.translated_text: 'Let it be further deliberated upon.' <s>Mādrī</s> says: 'Noble husband, to the best of my ability I will follow the noble husband.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> says: 'If so, this vow must be remembered by you.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 19]

children.text: ) tato bodhisatvaḥ pitaram abhigamya mūrdhnā praṇipatyovāca
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, approaching his father and bowing his head at his feet, said:

children.text: kṣamasva yat tāta mayāparāddhaṃ gajapradānaṃ prati pārthivendra /
children.translated_text: 'Forgive, dear father, the offense I have committed regarding the gift of the elephant, O lord of the earth.

children.text: eṣa prayāsyāmi purād araṇyaṃ kośakṣayo mā nṛpate tavābhūd // iti
children.translated_text: I shall now depart from the city to the forest — may there be no depletion of your treasury, O king.' Thus [he spoke].
Then
[continued]

children.text: putraviyogaviklavo rājā bāṣpoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭha uvāca: putra tiṣṭha nivartyatāṃ dānān mati
children.translated_text: the king, distraught from the separation from his son, with his throat choked by tears, said in a faltering voice: 'Son, stay! Let your resolve to give be turned back.'
[continued]
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:
'Even the earth with its mountains may revolve,

children.text: pradānān na tv ahaṃ cittaṃ nivarteyaṃ mahīpate //
children.translated_text: but I shall not turn my mind from giving, O lord of the earth.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 20]

children.text:
) tataḥ putraduhitṛkalatrasahitaḥ śokotkaṇṭhaiḥ paurajānapadaśatasahasrair anugamyamāno ratham adhiruhya tasmān nagaravarān nirjagāma.

children.translated_text: Then, accompanied by his son, daughter, and wife, followed by hundreds of thousands of citizens and country-folk distressed with grief, he mounted his chariot and departed from that excellent city.
[<s>Viśv</s> 21]

children.text:
) atha kaścit puruṣas taṃ ruditaparidevitaśabdaṃ śrutvā mahājanakāyaṃ ca nagaradvāreṇa nirgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvānyatamaṃ puruṣam uvāca: bhoḥ puruṣa kiṃkṛto 'yaṃ mahājanakāyasya rudanaśabda iti. sa uvāca: kiṃ bhavān na jānīte. yad asmad-
  deśāt svakān nṛpatinā svasutaḥ sudaṃṣṭro
  nirvāsyate sthiradhṛtir nirataḥ pradāne /
  sa prasthito vanam apetya saputradāraḥ
  paurāḥ
children.translated_text: Then a certain man, hearing those sounds of weeping and lamentation and seeing the great crowd going out through the city gate, said to another man: 'Sir, what is the reason for this weeping of the great crowd?' He replied: 'Do you not know? From our land, the king's own son <s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s> (Viśvantara), steadfast in resolve and devoted to giving, is being exiled by the king. He has departed with his sons and wife to the forest,
and
the citizens and servants weep most pitifully.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 22]

children.text: ) tato viśvantaro bodhisatvas tasmān nagaravarān nirgatān paurān yathānyāyam abhigamyovāca: nivartantu nivartantu bhavantaḥ. suciram api hi priyasaṃprayogo bhūtvāvaśyam evānte viyogāvasāno bhaviṣyati. vāsavṛkṣādhvapratiśrayabhūto 'pi bandhujanaviyogo 'vaśyabhāvī priyaviprayogaḥ. kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Viśvantara</s>, having duly approached the citizens who had come out from that excellent city, said: 'Turn back, turn back, good people! For even a long association with the beloved must inevitably end in separation. Even the parting of kinsmen, like travellers at the resting-place of a roadside tree, is an inevitable separation from the beloved. Therefore:

children.text: sarveṣu lokeṣv avagamya jantoḥ priyair viyogo bhavatīti matvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having understood in all the worlds that separation from the beloved befalls every creature,

children.text: kāryā bhavadbhir bhuvi sarvayatnaiḥ sthirāprakaṃpyā ca śamāya buddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: you should with every effort cultivate a mind firm, unshakeable, and directed toward peace.'
[<s>Viśv</s> 23]

children.text: ) atha triṃśadyojanātikrāntaṃ bodhisatvam avekṣyānyatamo brāhmaṇo 'bhigamyovāca: bhoḥ kṣatriyakumāra itas triṃśanmātrair yojanair adhiṣṭhānaṃ yato 'haṃ bhavato guṇaśravaṇād āgata iti. tad arhasi bhavān anena rathavareṇa me saphalaṃ śramaṃ kartum iti.
children.translated_text: Then a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having observed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who had already traversed thirty <s>yojanas</s>, approached him and said: 'O prince of the <s>kṣatriya</s> [caste], from a place only thirty <s>yojanas</s> hence is my dwelling, from where I have come upon hearing of your virtues. Therefore, you should make my effort fruitful with this excellent chariot.'

children.text: tato mādrī saṃjātāmarṣā niṣṭhurābhidhānena taṃ brāhmaṇam uvāca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mādrī</s>, seized with indignation, addressed that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> with harsh words:

children.text: aho dvijasyāsya sudāruṇā matir vane 'pi yo 'bhyarthayate nṛpātmajaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, how cruel is the intention of this twice-born, who solicits the prince even in the forest!

children.text: na nāma kāruṇyam ihāsya jāyate narendraputre nṛpatiśriyā cyute //
children.translated_text: Does no compassion arise in him here toward the prince who has fallen from royal splendor?'
[continued]

children.text: ṃ na khalu na khalu bhavatyā brāhmaṇaḥ paribhāṣaṇīyaḥ. kutaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Not so, not so! A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should certainly not be reproached by you, my lady. For:

children.text: yady ete na bhaveyur arthanadayo mādri pratigrāhakāḥ
children.translated_text: 'If these seekers of gifts were not present as recipients, <s>Mādrī</s>,

children.text: bodhiṃ kaḥ samavāpnuyād bhuvi naraḥ sarvapradānād ṛte /
children.translated_text: who among men could attain awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) without the giving of all?
By the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of supreme virtue always
attain, through giving and the rest, the supreme omniscience.'
